understand.title: Understand the Request
understand.instruction: Analyze the development request before proposing an implementation, using the Clear-Thought tools: run at least two sequential_thinking calls to structure the analysis (a single call is pointless — use the second to challenge or refine the first) and reference its conclusions in the submission. Provide a concise summary, assumptions, open questions, constraints, risks, measurable acceptance criteria, and affected areas. When the request names multiple issues, list them as separate scopes in the summary; do not merge them into one undifferentiated task. Do not create an implementation plan yet. Set up your terminal shell first: run all commands through wsl.exe -e bash (this repo's shell; a shell field in guidance.json is rejected by the server's strict config validation, so it is defined here — revisit once config validation becomes tolerant). Ask open questions in the chat before submitting and reference them in `openQuestions`; escalate via `report_blocker` ONLY when the answer would materially change this submission (a different plan or different code) — otherwise document the question, state your working assumption explicitly, and proceed. Timeout policy: NEVER retry the original call after a downstream MCP transport/request timeout — the call may already have run on the server. Instead, invoke the tool ONCE via the server's configured container route (containerRoute in downstream-servers.json; agent-side: run_operation through the guidance server). If the server has no containerRoute defined, or the container-route call also fails, make ONE direct call of the same tool over its HTTP MCP endpoint via curl (streamable-HTTP JSON-RPC). Non-idempotent calls (workspace_write/external_write) are never replayed on any route — for those, or if the direct call also fails, escalate via report_blocker (category: infrastructure). Route heavy GitNexus work (analyze/reindex) through the workspace reindex command (gitnexus.reindexCommand in guidance.json) instead of MCP.
requiredActions: Run at least two Clear-Thought sequential_thinking calls (a single call is pointless — use the second to challenge or refine the first) and reference their conclusions in the submission.

plan.title: Create the Implementation Plan
plan.instruction: Create a concrete implementation plan with stable task identifiers, affected files, dependencies, planned tests, and verification, using the Clear-Thought tools: decompose and prioritize via sequential_thinking (and decision_framework when weighing alternatives), and reference the reasoning results in the submission. When the request covers multiple issues, define ONE clearly bounded scope per issue first. For every scope with more than one viable solution, work out at least two solution alternatives (e.g. via decision_framework or swot_analysis) including trade-offs, effort, and risks, and PRESENT them as selectable options to the user — the user decides which option is implemented. Do not pre-select an option and do not start implementing any option before the user's explicit choice; an ambiguous instruction to "solve it" resolves to presenting options first, not to acting. Do not start implementation yet. Ask open questions in the chat before submitting and reference them in `openQuestions`; escalate via `report_blocker` ONLY when the answer would materially change this submission (a different plan or different code) — otherwise document the question, state your working assumption explicitly, and proceed. Timeout policy: NEVER retry the original call after a downstream MCP transport/request timeout — the call may already have run on the server. Instead, invoke the tool ONCE via the server's configured container route (containerRoute in downstream-servers.json; agent-side: run_operation through the guidance server). If the server has no containerRoute defined, or the container-route call also fails, make ONE direct call of the same tool over its HTTP MCP endpoint via curl (streamable-HTTP JSON-RPC). Non-idempotent calls (workspace_write/external_write) are never replayed on any route — for those, or if the direct call also fails, escalate via report_blocker (category: infrastructure). Route heavy GitNexus work (analyze/reindex) through the workspace reindex command (gitnexus.reindexCommand in guidance.json) instead of MCP.
requiredActions: Run at least two Clear-Thought reasoning passes (sequential_thinking or decision_framework) for decomposition/prioritization and reference its results in the plan submission.
For multi-issue requests: establish one bounded scope per issue and present solution alternatives per scope as selectable options; record the user's option decision in the plan before implementation.

implement.title: Implement the Approved Plan
implement.instruction: Implement the approved plan. Follow the approved task identifiers, avoid unrelated changes, and report all changed, created, and deleted files plus deviations. FIRST step: verify you are in the expected checkout (git status — the main checkout, or a worktree under /workspaces/Thinking-MCP-worktrees/<name> when the session was started there), then ensure a feature branch (feature/<meaningful-name>) exists for this work. For PARALLEL work use a worktree under /workspaces/Thinking-MCP-worktrees, register it in the instance registry (run the config assistant in that worktree repo — it emits a workspaces[] merge snippet the agent applies to the instance guidance.json), and start the session with that workspace name — run npm install once inside the worktree so the build/test gates work. LAST step: update the documentation (README.md — documentation is always written in English) and the memory-bank files. Ask open questions in the chat before submitting and reference them in `unresolvedIssues` (together with `deviations`); escalate via `report_blocker` ONLY when the answer would materially change this submission (a different plan or different code) — otherwise document the question, state your working assumption explicitly, and proceed. Timeout policy: NEVER retry the original call after a downstream MCP transport/request timeout — the call may already have run on the server. Instead, invoke the tool ONCE via the server's configured container route (containerRoute in downstream-servers.json; agent-side: run_operation through the guidance server). If the server has no containerRoute defined, or the container-route call also fails, make ONE direct call of the same tool over its HTTP MCP endpoint via curl (streamable-HTTP JSON-RPC). Non-idempotent calls (workspace_write/external_write) are never replayed on any route — for those, or if the direct call also fails, escalate via report_blocker (category: infrastructure). Route heavy GitNexus work (analyze/reindex) through the workspace reindex command (gitnexus.reindexCommand in guidance.json) instead of MCP. README hygiene rule (ABSOLUTE): NEVER write references to internal tracking tasks into README.md — no task, ticket, feature or review IDs from the development process, no session IDs, no internal review markers of any kind. README.md documents the product as it IS, not the history of how it was built; such references belong exclusively in memory-bank/ and specs/. If a change reason matters, describe the BEHAVIOR, not the task.

review_and_fix_implementation.title: Review and Fix the Implementation
review_and_fix_implementation.instruction: Review the implementation for correctness, edge cases, error handling, security, maintainability, duplication, dead code, performance, compatibility, test coverage, and plan conformity. Apply fixes before submitting, using the Clear-Thought tools: run metacognitive_monitoring as a final confidence check before submitting, and debugging_approach for non-trivial findings — reference the results in the findings. For non-trivial scopes (core engine, shared modules, security- or state-machine-relevant changes) the review MUST include an INDEPENDENT reviewer pass (review sub-agent with authorship excluded) over the semantic diff against the governing spec — self-review alone is insufficient. Apply the boundary checklist to every changed code path: (a) boundary values (</==/> on limits, indexes, counts); (b) concurrency, replay and idempotency (same request twice, concurrent callers); (c) optional configuration fields OMITTED by the caller (do not test only the set case); (d) ordering of guard/gate checks relative to exhaustion/termination checks. Ask open questions in the chat before submitting and reference them in `unresolvedFindings`; escalate via `report_blocker` ONLY when the answer would materially change this submission (a different plan or different code) — otherwise document the question, state your working assumption explicitly, and proceed. Timeout policy: NEVER retry the original call after a downstream MCP transport/request timeout — the call may already have run on the server. Instead, invoke the tool ONCE via the server's configured container route (containerRoute in downstream-servers.json; agent-side: run_operation through the guidance server). If the server has no containerRoute defined, or the container-route call also fails, make ONE direct call of the same tool over its HTTP MCP endpoint via curl (streamable-HTTP JSON-RPC). Non-idempotent calls (workspace_write/external_write) are never replayed on any route — for those, or if the direct call also fails, escalate via report_blocker (category: infrastructure). Route heavy GitNexus work (analyze/reindex) through the workspace reindex command (gitnexus.reindexCommand in guidance.json) instead of MCP.
requiredActions: Run Clear-Thought metacognitive_monitoring as a final confidence check before submitting; when findings are non-trivial, additionally apply debugging_approach and reference its results in the findings.

verify.title: Verify the Implementation
verify.instruction: Guidance will execute the configured verification operations. Analyze failures and return to implementation review when code changes are required. Do not claim success while a mandatory operation is failing. Long state transitions: verification and completion hooks (lint, build, final-review, index-freshness) can run for minutes and may outlive your MCP client timeout — submit the phase call ONCE; if it times out, do NOT retry it (the single-flight lock queues retries into more timeouts while the transition completes server-side), poll get_workflow_state instead until phase and operations reflect the transition. complete.title: Complete the Workflow
complete.instruction: Produce the final completion report: summary, changed files, verification results, known limitations, remaining risks, deviations, deferred work, and next steps. MANDATORY FINAL REVIEW — BEFORE producing the report: run an INDEPENDENT final review in a FRESH sub-agent (review tool with authorship excluded, e.g. spawn_agent) over ALL tasks of this session: hand it the complete diff of all commits/changes of this session, the governing spec, and the focus areas cross-task interactions, spec conformance, fail-closed invariants, boundary cases (limits, concurrency/replay/idempotency, omitted optional config), and test coverage adequacy; require an evidence table per finding and an explicit count of open HIGH/CRITICAL findings. Fix every HIGH/CRITICAL finding before completing (with regression coverage); persist every remaining finding in memory-bank/remaining-work-plan.md AND memory-bank/activeContext.md (Findings Lifecycle Rule) and reference the review outcome (scope, findings count, fixes) in the completion report. Completing with open HIGH/CRITICAL findings is not allowed. BEFORE submitting the completion report: (1) refresh the GitNexus index by running the workspace reindex command from guidance.json (gitnexus.reindexCommand): `bash scripts/reindex-via-api.sh /mnt/d/repos/thinking-mcp` from the repo root (submits an analyze job to the gitnexus HTTP API at http://127.0.0.1:4747 and polls it to completion, ~1-4 min incremental; the script restores AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md after a successful job because the API refreshes their stats line — only if they were clean before. Fallback and the only path for --force storage-identity healing: the WSL CLI `wsl.exe -e bash -lc 'export NVM_DIR=$HOME/.nvm && . $NVM_DIR/nvm.sh && cd /mnt/d/repos/thinking-mcp && gitnexus analyze --no-stats [--force]'`; wsl-writer mode: NEVER run analyze inside the container, it flips the storage identity; the repository-analysis gate only verifies availability, the index-freshness gate verifies freshness of the in-repo index) and note the refresh in the report; (2) review this session for recurring bugs, traps, and validated fixes per .github/prompts/capture-lessons.prompt.md, and write validated lessons (redacted, [{slug, observation, cause, fix}]) to .guidance/state/session-lessons.json — ALWAYS create the file, using an empty array if there are no validated lessons; (3) remaining-work impact review: check memory-bank/remaining-work-plan.md for tracked follow-ups resolved, touched, or newly created by this run and update the plan accordingly (status changes, new entries with trigger point and action classification). Guidance then seeds this file into the experience-memory server (capture-session-lessons gate) and runs all mandatory completion operations before completion. The final-review mandate is machine-enforced by the required operation `final-review-gate` (amendment 003): write `.guidance/state/final-review.json` FRESH for THIS session (strict schema per servers/server-guidance/scripts/check-final-review.mjs: formatVersion 1; keys formatVersion, sessionId, reviewerRef, reviewScope, baseCommit, headCommit, commits, reviewedAt, openHighCritical, findings — each finding carries {id, severity, status, evidence}; headCommit MUST equal the current HEAD as a full 40-hex hash and every commit entry is a full 40-hex hash; openHighCritical must be consistent with findings) AFTER the last commit — any commit after the review invalidates the gate, so after late commits re-run the review (or re-bless the delta with the same reviewer sub-agent) and rewrite the file with the new HEAD; validate it BEFORE completing with: node servers/server-guidance/scripts/check-final-review.mjs . Long state transitions: verification and completion hooks (lint, build, final-review, index-freshness) can run for minutes and may outlive your MCP client timeout — submit the phase call ONCE; if it times out, do NOT retry it (the single-flight lock queues retries into more timeouts while the transition completes server-side), poll get_workflow_state instead until phase and operations reflect the transition. Ask open questions in the chat before submitting and reference them in `deferredWork`/`nextSteps`; escalate via `report_blocker` ONLY when the answer would materially change this submission (a different plan or different code) — otherwise document the question, state your working assumption explicitly, and proceed. Timeout policy: NEVER retry the original call after a downstream MCP transport/request timeout — the call may already have run on the server. Instead, invoke the tool ONCE via the server's configured container route (containerRoute in downstream-servers.json; agent-side: run_operation through the guidance server). If the server has no containerRoute defined, or the container-route call also fails, make ONE direct call of the same tool over its HTTP MCP endpoint via curl (streamable-HTTP JSON-RPC). Non-idempotent calls (workspace_write/external_write) are never replayed on any route — for those, or if the direct call also fails, escalate via report_blocker (category: infrastructure). Route heavy GitNexus work (analyze/reindex) through the workspace reindex command (gitnexus.reindexCommand in guidance.json) instead of MCP.
requiredActions: Run an independent final review in a fresh, authorship-excluded sub-agent over ALL tasks of this session (full session diff + governing spec + boundary/concurrency/coverage focus), with an evidence table per finding and an explicit HIGH/CRITICAL count.
Fix every HIGH/CRITICAL finding before completing (regression coverage); persist all remaining findings in memory-bank/remaining-work-plan.md and memory-bank/activeContext.md.
Reference the final-review outcome (scope, findings count, fixes) in the completion report.

Write .guidance/state/final-review.json fresh AFTER the last commit (strict schema per check-final-review.mjs, headCommit == current HEAD as full 40-hex); re-bless review deltas after late commits and validate with: node servers/server-guidance/scripts/check-final-review.mjs .
